robots.name: FEDOR (Skybot F-850)
robots.note: Maker (NPO Android Technics, Magnitogorsk) describes FEDOR as an anthropomorphic rescue robot built under the FPV 'Rescuer' project, modified after handover to Roscosmos into Skybot F-850 for the Soyuz MS-14 flight (launched 2019-08-22, returned 2019-09-07). Nascent maker technical listings give 182 cm, 106 kg, 48 electromechanical drives, shoulder width 48 cm, about 1 h of continuous operation and walking speed about 4 km/h (1.11 m/s), Linux-based real-time OS; the ISS flight configuration is separately reported as 184 cm / 105 kg with 6 DOF per gripper and 10 kg per arm. CONFLICT recorded: press accounts of the 2019 flight give 160 kg for the ground model, so the weight depends on configuration; 106 kg is the maker listing figure. The legs were disabled in microgravity and the robot was teleoperated or ran predefined programs, so it is a research/demonstrator platform, never sold. No maker datasheet exists today - npo-at.com carries only news, so official_url points to the maker's FEDOR news item, and the 48 drives / 4 km/h / 1 h / 106 kg block is the most cited compilation of FEDOR listings (crediting Android Technics material), not a maker PDF. These figures are the least certain in this record.

Maker states 5.4 m armspan, 60 kg combined lift (Kawasaki release: 30 kg per arm), vertical reach >2.4 m, up to 16 cameras plus LiDAR, onboard 'supercomputer', operating 0-50 C, up to 1,500 m altitude (homepage says 5000 ft — minor conflict). Launched 17 Mar 2025; deployed for FedEx trailer loading and Sagawa Express validation.

robots.name: Diden Walker
robots.note: Scope review (#16, 2026-11-17): kept in scope and moved Humanoid -> Mobile platform. Diden's own product page lists 'Diden Walker - a biped work platform with magnetic feet' as a separate product from 'Diden Humanoid', so it is not a humanoid but a legged mobile platform that carries task modules (manipulator, inspection equipment). It walks on its own: maker blog says the lower body went from hardware to stable walking in about three months, successful on its first physical test (GTC 2026 and MARS 2026 posts). Feet are electro-permanent-magnet (EPM) with a differential ankle joint. Exhibitor listing gives launch date Dec 1, 2026.

robots.name: Nezha P01
robots.note: Maker product page (digit.com.cn/ProductsDetail/171.html): Nezha (星行侠) P01 is a highly customizable interaction robot with 'dual-mode, wheel and leg separable' mobility, hands-on teaching, an emotional-intelligence dialogue model, elevator control, long battery life and remote management through the JuHao app, and appearance/hands/voice customization. The maker publishes no height, weight, DoF, speed, runtime or price on the page, so specs stay empty. Manufacturer note: digit.com.cn is 数字华夏（深圳）科技有限公司 (Digital Huaxia); this record and digital-huaxia-xingxingxia-p02 are the same maker under two spellings, and 'Digit Robotics' comes from aggregator listings.

robots.name: Xialan S0
robots.note: No maker page names an 'Xialan S0'. Digital Huaxia's own catalogue (digit.com.cn, checked 2026-11-17) lists the 夏澜 line as S01/S02 and the newer R03, and the page an aggregator links for the S0 (digit.com.cn/ProductsDetail/170.html) renders no product content. The record's name and any specs trace to HumanoidStore and Humanoid.guide (which itself marks the entry 'not verified' and quotes 169 cm and 40+ DoF), so no field is filled. Manufacturer is Digital Huaxia (数字华夏), the same maker as the P02 record.

robots.name: XiaQi X02
robots.note: Maker product page (digit.com.cn/ProductsDetail/93.html): 夏起 X02 is a general-purpose interaction humanoid for marketing counters, showroom guidance, retail tours and reception, with multi-turn voice dialogue, natural facial expression and gestures, face tracking, lip detection and sound-source localisation, multi-language and Chinese-dialect conversation, and autonomous walking over marble, carpet and wooden floors in indoor spaces up to 100,000 m2. Maker publishes no height, weight, DoF, speed, runtime or price, so those fields stay empty. Manufacturer is Digital Huaxia (数字华夏); 'Digit Robotics' is the aggregator's name for the same company.

robots.name: Moxi
robots.note: Maker product page + Moxi 2.0 announcement (Oct 2025; rollout Aug 2026, NVIDIA Thor compute). Maker publishes no dimensions/weight/speed; aggregator figures (136 kg, 152 cm) left null. Category 'Indoor delivery' ok but it is a mobile manipulator (one arm).

robots.name: Xingzhe 2

The figures in the record came from the HumanoidStore import; third-party listings and a university lab page quote 170 cm, 32 kg, 30 DoF, 40 kg body load, 5-9 km/h and 6 h, which conflict with each other and with the values here (payload 2 kg, 20 DoF, 3 h). robots.name: SkyWalker II (Tianxingzhe 2)
robots.note: DOF conflict within maker material: launch said 55 DOF (with hands); basic-version table says 29 DOF excluding hands (used). A half-body fixed-base version (103 kg) also exists. Price from CNY 158,000 (no USD). Launched Sept 24, 2025.

robots.name: SA01
robots.note: Maker product page (meta description) states SA01 is an open-source, highly extensible bipedal robot platform with 12 DoF, large quick-release battery and in-house straight-knee gait; maker purchase page lists CNY 42,000 (price_usd left blank — CNY list only). Maker development history dates release 29 Jul 2024. It is a legs-only biped platform (arms optional add-ons per maker launch coverage). Detailed spec tab is JS-rendered and not readable; aggregator values (129-138 cm, 40 kg, 1 m/s, 2-4 h) not filled. Maker press release (CES 2025, PRNewswire) says ~40 kg and <200 W walking power — weight not filled since only an approximate PR figure.

robots.name: SA02
robots.note: EngineAI's own news page (10 Aug 2025) previews SA02 as 'Everyone's First Humanoid Robot' starting at CNY 38,500 (about USD 5,300) at the 2025 World Robot Conference. EngineAI has no SA02 product page (its current product line is PM01, T800, JS01, SE01 and S2), and the 1 .25 m / 25 kg build and DoF count come only from the launch spec sheet as reproduced in trade press, which quotes both 26 and 28 DoF - so dof is left empty and the conflicting counts noted. Payload, speed, runtime and battery are not published.

robots.name: ExR-2.5
robots.note: ExRobotics (Delft) product page: ATEX/IECEx Zone 1 + UL certified, -40 to +55 C, up to 2 km per charge, mission 2-6 h (runtime_h = upper bound 6), autonomous inductive docking, 4G/5G, 100+ robots deployed. Locomotion not stated in maker page text (US distributor MicroWatt calls it tracked) - left out; verify before setting Tracked. Speed 2 km/h appears in maker text seen only in a search excerpt (old /our-products page now 404), so max_speed_mps left out (would be 0.56). Weight 110-140 kg only on aggregators. Software via partner (page names Korial; older material Energy Robotics).

robots.name: FX Aegis Hyper
robots.note: Launched Sept 19, 2026. Maker says legged quadruped; Forbes calls it wheeled-legged (wrong). 85 kg is maximum payload; the shop page lists 20 kg (44 lb) rated, and 2.5 h runtime with payload.

robots.name: FX Navi
robots.note: Faraday Future store page: 12-DOF quadruped, ~8 kg, max 2 m/s, 34 cm obstacle, ~2 h runtime, battery ~0.2-0.3 kWh (range, battery_wh left out), Linux, open low-level interface + Python SDK, perception/compute via paired smartphone (AI compute 'not disclosed'), MSRP $1,990. Dimensions conflict: store lists L x W x H 112 mm (308 mm standing) x 298 x 515 mm, launch release says 46.5 x 20 x 51.5 cm - dimensions left out. Launched 16 Jun 2026.

robots.note: Maker specs read from Figure's own 2023 homepage (via Wayback Machine, figure.ai no longer shows Figure 01): height 5'6" (1676 mm), 60 kg, 20 kg payload, 5 h runtime, 1.2 m/s, electric. Current figure.ai features Figure 03; Figure 01 superseded by Figure 02 (2024) -> status Discontinued (retired prototype/pilot, never sold). DoF figures in aggregators conflict (16 vs 40+ vs 41) and are not maker-stated - not filled.

robots.name: Figure 02
robots.note: Figure's own homepage at the time (Wayback snapshot, 31 Dec 2024) lists Figure 02 as 5'6" (1676 mm), 70 kg, 20 kg payload, 5 h runtime, 1.2 m/s, electric - the maker values stored here. The 6 Aug 2024 press release covers the 2.25 kWh torso battery, 6 onboard RGB cameras, 4th-gen hands with 16 DoF each (per hand, not total), onboard VLM and 3x compute vs Figure 01; tested at BMW Spartanburg. Figure began retiring F.02 after Figure 03 (Oct 2025) and announced fleet decommissioning on 30 Sep 2026 (a few units kept in storage) -> Discontinued. Total body DoF is not published by Figure (aggregators give 35/41) - left empty.

robots.name: AICO 2
robots.note: Flexiv lists two AICO 2 variants: AICO 2-4 (2×4 kg payload, 281 kg, 6 h, dual-wheel differential) and AICO 2-10 (2×10 kg, 395 kg, 4 h). Variant-specific fields left null.

robots.name: Max 1500-L Slim
robots.note: Confirmed by ForwardX launch press releases (Nov 2023) and Max Series page. Naming: current maker page lists the model as 'Max 1500-L' (image labelled 'Max 1500-L Slim CE'); 'Slim' was the 2023 launch name. Width conflict: current maker page says 800 mm, older 2024 brochure/distributor (Roboware) says 850 mm - maker's current page value used. Max speed (1.1 m/s loaded / 1.5 m/s empty) and 48V 72Ah battery appear only on a Japanese distributor page - not filled. Sensors per maker page: 4 LiDAR, wide-angle cameras, optional 0-2 3D cameras, downward QR camera, odometer, IMU. One reseller (Logicbus) lists a non-CE variant as discontinued.

robots.name: FoxBot ATL (Mk3)
robots.note: Current model is FoxBot ATL Mk3 (autonomous trailer loader/unloader; Mk3 added loading, auto-adjusting fork tines, expanded sensors - maker blog Mar 2025). It is a retrofitted standard Class 1 three-wheel counterbalance electric forklift (manual driving still possible) - category is really autonomous forklift, not a typical AMR. Maker 1-pager: H 88 in (2235 mm), W 53 in (1346 mm), length with forks 110 in (2794 mm), 3,000 lb payload (1,361 kg), 16-18 h battery life (runtime_h=16; a Jan 2024 maker post said 18-20 h - conflict), operates down to -10 °C. Weight: Mark II user manual lists 7,189 lb excl. battery (excerpt only, older generation) - not filled. Top speed 2.35 m/s appears only on an aggregator - not filled.

robots.name: Futuring F2
robots.note: A wheeled dual-arm home robot per photos and press (maker text doesn't state the base type, so locomotion left blank); not a biped (some aggregators wrongly list 28-DOF biped specs). Released April 2026; maker price CNY 36,000 (no USD). Payload 3 kg at end effector; runtime >8 h.

robots.name: GoMate
robots.note: Maker sources opened 2026-11-17: GAC Group's official WeChat post on the 26 Dec 2024 launch calls GoMate a full-size wheel-legged humanoid ('全尺寸的轮足人形机器人') with 38 DoF and an industry-first variable wheel-foot structure combining four-wheel-foot and two-wheel-foot modes (~1.4 m stable on four, up to 1.75 m standing on two); gacgroup.com history page states 'GoMate行业首创可变轮足'. Runtime up to 6 h on GAC's all-solid-state battery. Locomotion is WHEEL-LEGGED, not bipedal. height_mm left null because it depends on the mode. GoMate Mini is a separate 4th-gen model. | Maker release opened 2026-11-17: GAC Group's own launch article for the 3rd-generation GoMate (2024-12-26, 2024 China Robot Network annual conference) - full-size WHEEL-LEGGED humanoid, 38 DoF, industry-first variable wheel-foot structure (four-wheel mode ~1.4 m, two-wheel standing 1.75 m), solid-state battery, runtime up to 6 h, self-developed hands/drives/motors, about 80% lower energy consumption than comparable products. gacgroup.com/cn/about/history (opened) records the same 2024-12-26 launch. Height stored is the two-wheel standing figure (1.75 m); four-wheel mode is ~1.4 m. DoF = 38 maker-stated. No weight/payload published, so those stay null. Earlier failure of gacgroup.com news detail pages (HTTP 408) is why this record was unconfirmed. GAC also has a 4th-gen 'GoMate Mini' (1.7 m, 27 DoF, 8 h) per its HKEX filing - a different model.

robots.name: Nexo
robots.note: Wheeled-not-legged: dual-arm humanoid upper body on a wheeled base. Unveiled at WRC, Aug 2026. Aggregator figures (168 cm, 85 kg, 200 TOPS, 5 km/h) conflict with Galaxea's page (1,700 mm, 2.5 m/s, 2000/700 TOPS); maker kept.

robots.name: G1
robots.note: Maker spec panel (galbot.com/g1): max height 1730 mm (leg lift 650 mm), 92.5 kg, payload 5 kg per arm / 10 kg total at the wrist, 21 DoF (neck 2 + arms 7x2 + waist 3 + legs 2, excluding chassis and end effectors), 8 h working time with 3.5 h adapter charging, 48 V 30 Ah battery (=1440 Wh, derived from V x Ah), IP54, 4-wheel omnidirectional chassis 600/600/625 mm, 1.5 m/s, NVIDIA AGX Orin 64GB / 275 TOPS, 0-40 C. No price on the maker site; HumanoidStore's 87,000 USD list price was removed (aggregator).

robots.name: Poppy Humanoid
robots.note: Maker repository (poppy-project/poppy-humanoid): open-source 3D-printed humanoid, 25 Robotis Dynamixel actuators, about 60% of the BOM cost, full build 8,000-9,000 USD, Raspberry Pi 3/4 on-board, pypot Python library, GPL v3 / CC BY-SA. The project site (www.poppy-project.org, docs.poppy-project.org) returned HTTP 500 on 2026-11-17, so the 83 cm / 3.5 kg figures on its v1.0.2 page could not be re-opened and height/weight were left empty instead of carrying the aggregator's 840 mm / 3.5 kg values. Generation Robots is a distributor, not the designer. The 11,193 USD price was an aggregator conversion of a EUR list price and was removed.

robots.name: 铅球 SP1 (Qianqiu SP1)
robots.note: Official product name is 铅球 SP1 (qiānqiú, 'shot put') - 'Qiuqiu' was a wrong romanisation, so the id keeps the old slug for link stability. Explosion-proof inspection quadruped for Zone 1/2 gas atmospheres (Ex d IIC T6 Gb), IP66, 50 kg continuous payload, 35° slope, 4 h full-load runtime. Weight stated '≤100 kg'; runtime '≥4 h'.

robots.name: Spirit 40
robots.note: Product page ghostrobotics.io/spirit-40 now returns 404 and the maker's site offers only Vision 60 (checked 2026-11-17), so the 2020 Spirit 40 is treated as discontinued; the maker never states it in words. Exists per Ghost Robotics' official YouTube channel. No official spec page reachable; aggregator specs (12 kg, 2 m/s) left null.

robots.name: Laborer M1
robots.note: Maker parameter table (glroad.com, 劳动者M1): height 187 cm, mass 86 kg, dual-arm payload 50 kg (combined, test conditions not stated), moving speed >1.2 m/s (field = 1.2 m/s, lower bound), battery 22 Ah (voltage not published), runtime 2 h, 27 whole-body DoF (6 per leg, 1 head; the table's single-arm figure is inconsistent with the maker's own diagram showing 7-DoF arms), peak joint torque 430 N.m, dual encoders, arm-end accuracy printed illegibly on the page. Released 20 Aug 2026 with the C1. C1 is a different, much smaller robot.

robots.name: Mini Hi (Xiaohai)
robots.note: Maker pages conflict: Chinese page 810 mm / 21.5 kg / 23 DOF / 1.15 m/s (used); older English page 890 mm / 20 kg / 27 DOF; WRC 2026 listing 82 cm / 17 kg. A 25-DOF Hi Pro exists. Runtime stated as '>1 h'.

robots.name: Mini Pi Plus
robots.note: Maker page (hightorque.cn/pi-plus): standing height 680 mm, 15.15 kg with battery, 22 DoF, payload 10 kg, max joint torque 21 N.m, 24 V working voltage, modular open architecture, SDK, multi-channel CAN FD, jumping and gait walking. Maker store: Base 6,000 USD (RK3588, 15.4 kg) and Pro 8,000 USD (Jetson Orin NX + RealSense D435i, 15.6 kg), battery 21.6 V 4500 mAh (=97 Wh derived), 60 min operating time, 1.1 m/s, ROS 1 + SDK. Conflict: 24 V on the product page vs 21.6 V / 4500 mAh pack in the store spec. The 8,000 USD Pro price was not used for price_usd (Base configuration is recorded).

robots.name: Q3-600D
robots.note: Model-specific maker page opened 2026-11-17: Hikrobot's own LMR wiki page 'Q3-600D 主推车型技术参数' (no longer snippet-only). Maker-stated: 950x650x250 mm, 134 kg, rated load 600 kg, lift 60 mm electric (20 mm/s), platform 850x600 mm, ground clearance 25 mm, differential drive, rated speed 2.0 m/s empty / 1.8 m/s loaded, rotation 200/100 deg/s, positioning +/-10 mm / +/-1 deg, 3 deg slope, front laser + front/rear bumper + e-stop, QR/L-SLAM navigation, LiFePO4 48 V (1500 cycles), 8 h runtime at rated duty, charge <=1.5 h, rear charging, WiFi, touch screen. Distributor sheets list 132 kg and 9 h; maker page 134 kg / 8 h stored. Category note: natural-feature (L-SLAM/V-SLAM) navigation option makes 'AMR' arguably better than 'AGV'.

robots.name: ASIMO
robots.note: Specs are the 2011 'all-new ASIMO' per Honda (130x45x34 cm, 48 kg, 57 DoF, 9 km/h, 40 min). Earlier versions differ (2000: 120 cm/43 kg). Honda ended ASIMO development in 2018 (Nikkei report of 28 Jun 2018; Honda said humanoid research continues) -> Discontinued.

robots.name: iggyRob
robots.note: Maker product page: 101 kg, maximum component weight 1.5 kg, AMR basis ReBeLMove Pro, two ReBeL-6DOF-03 arms (664 mm reach, 2 kg per arm), suction pad plus ReBeL gripper, LiDAR and 3D cameras, up to 8 h per charge, igus Robot Control, ROS 2 interface, CE and VDE 5050 fleet approval. Launch price 47,999 EUR (Iggy Rob Industrial, 2025); Iggy Rob Home from 55,000 EUR (Jun 2026). The 58,024 USD list figure was an aggregator conversion and was removed.

robots.name: igus Humanoid Open Platform (HOP)
robots.note: Developed by University of Bonn (NimbRo/AIS) in cooperation with igus; open hardware released 2015, won the 2016 HARTING Open Source Prize. Not igus's current product: igus now sells the wheeled 'Iggy Rob' humanoid (2025), a different robot.

robots.name: Daksha Gen-2
robots.note: Maker page (/daksha-mini, 'Daksha Gen-2 - Mobile Humanoid Robot'; spec text on the DakshaMini product page): 15 Ah / 0.972 kWh battery giving about 3 h, rated arm payload 7 kg with 15 kg peak, head-mounted stereo camera with wide field of view plus wrist cameras and an IMU, remote emergency stop, NVIDIA Isaac GR00T open models and reference workflows. Payload field = 7 kg rated (15 kg peak). Height, mass, DoF and price are not published on the page checked. Note that 'TARA Gen 2' is the older DAKSHA semi-humanoid (190 cm, 120-150 kg, 27 DoF), a different model.

robots.name: inVia Picker
robots.note: inVia product page, system overview and blog: 40 lb payload, reach up to 8 ft, hot-swappable batteries >10 h. Speed/dimensions only on aggregators, left null.

robots.name: ergoCub
robots.note: Research humanoid from IIT (with INAIL funding), evolution of iCub; unveiled publicly Sept 2023 (IIT 20th anniversary). Maker-stated: 1.5 m, 55.7 kg, ~10 kg load (payload approximate), Intel RealSense depth camera, LiDAR, new-generation force-torque sensors, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier + 11th-gen Intel i7, OLED 2K face screen. DoF '54' comes from a design-award page (not IIT) - not filled; a Nature MI paper figure reportedly shows 56.7 kg (conflict, maker 55.7 kg kept). Not for sale.

robots.name: HyQ
robots.note: Maker page (Dynamic Legged Systems): 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.98 m with legs stretched, 80 kg with external hydraulics and 100 kg with the onboard supply, 12 hydraulically actuated DoF, running up to 2 m/s, stereo camera and lidar, PC104 Pentium running real-time Linux. The 2011 design paper gives 70 kg / 91 kg for the same machine, so the maker's page figures are kept and the paper's are recorded here as the conflict.

robots.name: IIT iCub
robots.note: Maker material (RobotCub leaflet and the iCub paper by IIT/Univ. of Genoa): 104 cm, 53 DoF (head 6, arms 7x2, hands 9x2, legs 6x2, waist 3), 25 kg without battery / 29 kg with battery (IIT facility documentation; weight field = 29 kg), 48 V on-board battery pack, ~4,000-point capacitive skin, YARP/ROS middleware, GPL/FDL open hardware and software. Earlier leaflets quote 22 kg. The 280,625 USD price was an aggregator conversion of a 250,000 EUR figure and was removed - IIT sells iCubs to labs by quotation.

robots.name: Kargo
robots.note: Wheeled dual-arm humanoid (differential base). DoF: EN page 20, CN page 22; cameras 2 (EN) / 4 (CN). payload_kg = per-arm load. IP20 refers to control cabinet.

robots.note: Maker site lists M-Bot only as 'Compact 2.5' humanoid' (~762 mm, converted from 2.5 ft), 'Coming soon', no specs or release date; it never appears in the maker's achievements timeline, so it likely never shipped. robots.name: Z-Bot
robots.note: Maker site lists Z-Bot as 'Tabletop 1.5' humanoid' (~457 mm, converted from 1.5 ft) and Z-Bot V2 (Jan 2025, used in Stanford CS courses); Z-Bot V1 Nov 2024 was 3D-printable for under $350. Open-source K-OS (Rust) with Python SDK.

robots.note: Maker product page: 154 cm, 56 kg, 17,000 mAh 48 V battery (=816 Wh, derived), 2.5 h charge, 53 DOF per the maker docs (legs 6 x 2, arms 7 x 2, waist 3, neck 2, hands 11 x 2 where each hand has 6 active + 5 passive DoF); the marketing page's DOF list omits the hand joints and adds up to 43. CONFLICT: the developer docs (v1.0.5 and v2.1.1, updated 2026-06-24) give 60 kg and 1540 x 440 x 300 mm while the product page gives 56 kg; the product page figure is used here and the docs figure is recorded. Max joint torque 150 Nm, 6 kg payload with both arms, Linux/Cyclone DDS with C++ and Python APIs, RGB stereo + RealSense D435i depth head cameras and per-hand RGB cameras, 6-axis IMU, Wi-Fi AP and BLE, force limiting and collision detection, emergency stop, industrial Class A, sold in Korea with global inquiries. Max speed and runtime are not published. ROBROS reported building 36 units and selling 18 by end-August 2026.

robots.name: Suyuan 2.0
robots.note: Maker statements conflict on DOF: Shanghai Electric's own LinkedIn post (2026-07-18) says 43 degrees of freedom, while the company's WAIC 2026 release (2026-07-24, via PR wire) says 41; 41 is used here as the later figure and 43 is recorded as the conflict (Jiefang Daily also reported 43, with 12 DOF per hand against 6 in the first generation). The maker confirms multimodal vision on head and torso and a dual-battery hot-swap system. Height 175 cm and weight 65 kg come from Jiefang Daily's July 2026 report, not from a maker release, and the 5 kg single-arm payload was quoted by Shanghai Electric staff at the June 2026 debut; 10 units were reported working on Shanghai Electric's own production lines (warehouse and electrical-cabinet tasks), hence Pilot. No speed, battery capacity, runtime, compute or price is published.

robots.name: Forerunner K2
robots.note: Maker press releases: Forerunner K2 launched at GITEX GLOBAL 2024 (Oct 2024) and described at WAIC 2025 as 175 cm, 75 kg, 52 DoF (22 hand DoF), 2.33 kWh battery for 8 h operation with 1 h charging, bimanual payload 25-30 kg and 15 kg per hand, 11-DoF tactile hands with 96 contact points per fingertip, 2 head DoF, 100 TOPS on-board. Pre-sales opened with three configurations (Bipedal Basic, Bipedal Developer, Wheeled Developer) from 248,000 CNY. The 34,000 USD price was an aggregator figure and was removed. No maker product-domain page was found, so official_url is empty.

robots.name: DUCO
robots.note: The record is brand-level ('DUCO'), and DUCO is the embodied-intelligence brand of SIASUN subsidiary Zhongke Xinsong (中科新松), so no single model's specs were written into the record. Maker product page for the 类人形 series: BR-MR73A wheeled humanoid and BR-DR73 half-body (fixed pedestal) share dual 7-DOF force-controlled arms with 630 mm working radius, +/-0.05 mm repeatability and 800 mm/s TCP speed; the table gives one variant 17 DOF (head 2, arms 7 x 2, waist 1) and 24 DOF (head 2, arms 7 x 2, waist 4, chassis 4) for the other, 5 kg per arm (8 kg with both), 800-1,450 mm or 800-2,000 mm working height, Orin AGX 200/275 TOPS, head depth camera plus front/rear torso cameras and microphone array, 1.2 m/s with laser SLAM and +/-5 mm docking, ROS 2 and Python SDK, one variant running continuously with no battery and the other giving about 6 h. CONFLICT: the maker's blog gives the BR-MR73A a 3 kg arm payload and 1.2 m/s while the product table gives 5 kg per arm / 8 kg dual, and the table's variant columns do not line up with the model names, so the per-model mapping is uncertain. The humanoid.guide figures (~30-35 DOF, ~150-160 cm, ~90-110 kg, 85,000 USD) are unverified and were not used.

robots.name: Aiqiu
robots.manufacturer: Sichuan Embodied AI Robot Innovation Center
robots.note: Maker: Sichuan Embodied Humanoid Robot Technology Co. (EIR, 四川具身人形机器人科技有限公司), Chengdu, founded 2024-09 by University of Electronic Science and Technology professors, whose lineup also includes the Skywalker full-size humanoid and the Tianxun industrial quadruped. Aiqiu was previewed 2025-12-16 as the world's first emotion-interaction humanoid, with a 3D ultra-short-throw projected face (a first in China), the ELA Emotion-Language-Action model and a multimodal emotion engine; the new generation was launched and put on sale at WRC 2026 (August 2026) in an interaction edition for finance, culture-tourism, education and commercial service and a motion-control edition for universities and developers, from CNY 98,000. No maker spec sheet is public and eir.com.cn did not respond, so height, weight, DOF, payload, speed, battery and runtime stay empty; the 143 cm / 38 kg / 32 DOF / 2 h figures circulating on aggregator sites were not used. Marked unconfirmed because the only maker-side sources are an exhibitor entry and press coverage, not a datasheet.

robots.name: i7 Pro
robots.note: Maker product page: 1,560-1,705 mm (H) x 548 mm (W) x 670 mm (L) - the minimum height is entered - 165 kg, 18 active DOF excluding hands (arm 7 x 2, waist lift 1, chassis 3), 703 mm single-arm span, 1,000 mm max working radius, 6 kg payload with the arm extended and 12 kg bent (6 kg entered), +/-0.05 mm repeatability, 3 N force-control accuracy, chassis speed 1.5 m/s with four-wheel steering and four-wheel drive, 650 mm lift stroke, two batteries totalling 1,650 Wh with about 4-5 h runtime (4.5 h entered), hot-swap or dock charging at 2 h per bay, four-wheel chassis, head RGBD + 3 fisheye, wrist RGBD x 2, LiDAR x 2, 8 ultrasonic sensors, 4 x 2 microphone array, 8.8-inch display, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/4G/5G. The maker's retail-logistics page describes SimpleWAM sorting at over 1,500 items/hour on DRIVE Thor-U. Maker notes specs describe the i7 configuration and delivered units may differ.

robots.name: ToddlerBot
robots.note: Maker paper (CoRL 2025) and project site: 0.56 m tall, 3.4 kg, 30 active DOF excluding end effectors (7 per arm, 6 per leg, 2 neck, 2 waist), 2 fisheye cameras, IMU in the chest, speaker, 2 microphones, Jetson Orin NX 16GB, entirely 3D-printed with off-the-shelf Dynamixel motors, total BOM cost under USD 6,000, design under CC BY-NC-SA and code under MIT, with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and a teleoperation interface; two end-effector designs (parallel jaw gripper and compliant palm) swap in two minutes. The catalog's earlier payload (1.484 kg), max speed (0.25 m/s) and runtime (0.32 h) were HumanoidStore figures that the maker paper does not state in those terms, so they were removed rather than kept on an aggregator's authority.

robots.name: Nova
robots.note: Maker page and its specification sheet (a Nova reference configuration): 5 ft (about 152 cm), 70 lb (31.8 kg), wheeled differential drive with zero-radius turning, 0.8-1.2 m/s (1.2 m/s entered as the upper bound), 2-3 kg arm payload (3 kg entered), depth cameras plus RGB camera and IMU, on-device LLM with cloud fallback, voice interaction in English/Spanish/Italian, interactive touchscreen, target runtime up to 10-12 h configuration-dependent (11 h entered as the midpoint), 3 h charge, indoor commercial spaces, Wi-Fi with OTA updates and a monitoring dashboard. Launched December 2025 when the company moved from bipedal testing to a wheeled base with two 7-DOF arms. DOF total, battery capacity and price are not stated.

robots.name: Memo
robots.note: Maker site: 170 cm resting at about 4 ft with arms reaching 7 ft (about 210 cm), 170 lb (77 kg), rolling base with passive stability and no legs, about 4 h runtime and 1 h recharge, speed limited by software to roughly half human pace (about 1 m/s), a single camera under the hat brim, compliant control, and DOF given only as a breakdown - arms 2 x 7, hands 2 x 4, torso 1, lower body 4, which sums to 27 (the total is our sum, not the maker's). Hands are IP67 and lower arms IP66. Not for sale: invite-only 2026 beta for Founding Families, and the maker says a hand-built unit costs about USD 20,000 today with retail pricing to be announced, so no price is entered. The earlier 6 kg payload figure is not maker-stated and was removed.

robots.name: FlexSwift MAX
robots.note: Maker's current lineup (syriusrobotics.com -> syriustechnology.com) sells this pick-assist AMR as 'FlexSwift MAX' alongside FlexPorter GO/DO; the earlier listing used 'FlexSwift'. The 100 kg payload is stated on a Syrius-owned page (Japan site, FlexSwift MAX); other specs appear only on distributor or aggregator pages and are left null.

robots.name: T4-C
robots.note: The maker's spec table (poster on TetraBOT's CDN, 2026-07-16) covers four variants that differ in size, weight and DoF, so variant-dependent fields are left empty: Lite 630x840x260 mm, 18 kg, 10 DoF (5 per arm), external power only; Pro 630x840x260 mm, 20 kg, 14 DoF (7 per arm), external power; Max 570x1470x550 mm folded / 570x1870x550 mm extended, 48 kg, 13 DoF (5 per arm, 1 waist, 2 base), about 1.5 h on battery; Ultra same size, 50 kg, 17 DoF (7 per arm, 1 waist, 2 base), about 1.5 h. Shared: 82 Nm peak shoulder torque, 3 kg hand payload, 740 mm arm span, 8-core CPU at 6 TOPS with optional Orin, 8-microphone array, 6 W speaker, Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2, binocular head camera with optional wrist depth camera, base LiDAR on Max and Ultra.

robots.name: T170A "Yao Guang"
robots.note: RENAME: 'Yao Guang' (瑶光) is the name of a unit of Ti5's second-gen T170A humanoid launched at WAIC 4 Jul 2024 (maker news ti5robot.com/h-nd-39.html, read via search excerpt; page now 404). Maker release: 1.7 m, 48 kg, 44 DoF, 5 kg single-hand load, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB, LiDAR + binocular cameras. Maker's current English site (ti5robotics.com) lists T170A and newer T170A V2/T170C/T140A; a 2025 maker EN page (seen in excerpts) also cites dual-arm load 20-40 kg, five RealSense cameras, 6-mic array — newer config, not filled. Status left blank (superseded by T170A V2 likely). Maker model page opened 2026-11-17 (ti5robotics.com .../T170A.html): 48 kg, 1.5 m arm span, 44 active DoF, 32 joint motors, single-arm load 3 kg, hand 6 active DoF (0.5 kg standard / 3 kg flagship), 18-bit encoders, 48 V 10 Ah battery, CAN/EtherCAT, dual-arm API; standard model Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB, flagship Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB dev kit + RealSense D435i + 2x six-axis force sensors. CONFLICT: the 2024 WAIC release (now 404) said 5 kg single-hand load; the current maker page says 3 kg single-arm, which is stored. Height 1.7 m comes from the T170A naming/2024 release; the current page's parameter table omits height. Note the maker site serves swapped pages (T170A-V2.html returns the T170A table), so page-to-model mapping was taken from the printed heading.

robots.name: TITAN-XIII
robots.note: Figures are from the laboratory's own publications - ROBOMECH Journal 2016 (Kitano, Hirose, Horigome, Endo) and IROS 2013: standard posture 220 x 550 x 300 mm, 5.65 kg including the LiFePO4 battery (26.4 V, 1100 mAh), 12 DoF (3 per leg), maximum walking speed 1.38 m/s at COT 1.76, and a 5 kg walking payload (20 kg when statically supported). Published size differs between papers - 420 x 420 x 300 mm in the IROS 2013 table and 600 x 600 x 300 mm in the ROBOMECH 2013 table - and the ROBOMECH 2013 table lists 1.0 m/s and a 1 kg payload, so the 2016 journal values are recorded here. robots.note: Maker = UCLA RoMeLa (academic research lab, not a company). robots.name: CartConnect500
robots.note: Confirmed by Zebra MODEX 2022 press release (payload 600 lb). Detailed specs only in Zebra-authored brochure hosted by resellers; dims/weight taken from that Zebra brochure (cssi.com copy) - treat as maker document on third-party host. Earlier 2020 Fetch brochure stated 500 lb payload. Re-checked 2026-11-17: no CartConnect500 product page exists on zebra.com any more (zebra.com/us/en/products/robotics.html returns 404; Zebra sold its robotics automation business - formerly Fetch Robotics - to Skild AI, closed 2026-03-27 per Zebra's 10-Q, so the Fetch/Zebra AMR product pages are gone), so the Zebra-authored AMR solution guide (2021, sampled above) stays the source. That guide's spec table gives max speed 1.5 m/s, ~9 h runtime, 2x SICK 30 m/275 deg scanners and 8x 3D cameras, now filled. CONFLICT kept in the record: the same guide's spec table prints 'Maximum Payload Weight 800 lb (362.9 kg)' while its body text and Zebra's 2022 press release say loads up to 600 lb (272 kg); 272 kg is stored.

robots.name: Jupiter
robots.note: Official Zeroth store page: reservation price $89,999 (list $131,999), US shipping; maker entity Suzhou JoyIn Intelligent Technology (Zeroth). Height, weight, joints and runtime come from the maker-supplied IFA 2026 exhibitor listing for Zeroth: 165 cm, 58 kg, 25 joints, 22 hand articulation points (10 per hand), footprint about 2 m2, 2 h 20 min of active use -> 1650 mm, 58 kg, 25 DoF, 2.33 h. Zeroth publishes no payload or top speed for Jupiter (store and product pages have no specification table) - left empty; humanoid.guide's 60 kg / 30 DoF / 4 h / 6 kg are not maker-stated and were not used.

robots.name: Sean (N1 / 小恩)
robots.note: Rename/correction: 'Sean' is the English name of Zeroth's N1 (小恩) home collaboration robot - NOT a 155 cm bipedal humanoid as aggregators claim. Maker-supplied IFA 2026 exhibitor copy: wheeled compact home robot, 30 kg, ~0.2 m2 footprint, 14 joints (telescopic left arm 4 joints, right cable-driven arm 7 joints, 3-finger gripper), 2-3 h active use, reach floor to countertop; detachable right arm. Launched at AWE 12 Mar 2026. No product page on zeroth0.com. Aggregator figures (155 cm, 45 kg, 16 DoF, 3 km/h) are not maker-stated. Re-checked 2026-11-17: zeroth0.com opened - its product menu now lists M1 / M1 EDU, W1 and Jupiter only (products/m1, /w1, /jupiter); there is still no N1/Sean product page. The maker-supplied IFA Berlin exhibitor profile remains the only maker document with figures (30 kg, ~0.2 m2 footprint, 14 joints, 2-3 h, floor-to-countertop reach).
